newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court rejects Air France appeal in CDC state aid case.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects Air France appeal in CDC state aid case.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance upheld on Thursday the 1994 European Commission decision to order the re-payment by Air France of 1.5 billion francs ($288 million) granted by French state-controlled Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC).

The court dismissed Air France's plea to overrule the Commission's characterisation as state aid the subscription by CDC to the airline in 1993 of nearly 750 million francs in bonds redeemable into shares and an equal amount of progressive interest subordinated notes.

The Commission concluded in 1994 that the subscriptions amounted to state aid on the grounds that a reasonable private investor would not have injected that amount of money in Air France in view of its poor financial performance.
Air France argued that, even if the subscriptions involved state aid, the Commission should have given the airline the choice between reimbursement and correction of the subscription terms.

But the court ruled that because the securities had already been purchased, the Commission did not have to quantify the advantage which Air France gained in relation to market conditions. The court said to to do so would require an onerous and complex economic appraisal given the nature of the instruments at stake.
The Commission's 1994 decision against the CDC subscription was taken at the same time it cleared a 20-billion-franc rescue package for the French troubled airline.

The approved decision was challenged in the court by a certain number of European rival airlines, including British Airways and British Midland, who argue the conditions put on the aid were not enough to compensate for unfair competition. The court has yet to rule on that decision.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)
